_about: What a '.dtls' glyph -- the dotless cut of i or j in a styled math font --
resolves to on the glyphs2u side.  Unicode encodes dotless i and j only as
U+0131/U+0237 (plain) and U+1D6A4/U+1D6A5 (italic); there is no
double-struck, fraktur, monospace or sans-serif dotless i.  So every one of
these glyphs forces a choice between two things it cannot keep at once:
the DOT being absent, or the font view (double-struck, fraktur, ...).
Deriving it from base+properties alone always sacrificed the font view,
which is what made the existing lua tables inconsistent.
'dotted' keeps the font view and gives up the dot -- it resolves to the
styled letter WITH its dot, composed from base 'i'/'j' and the font's own
properties.  That target is not guessed: for all 26 stix cases it comes out
exactly equal to the codepoint the glyph's own name states (u1D55A.dtls ->
U+1D55A MATHEMATICAL DOUBLE-STRUCK SMALL I), so the font's designers and
this derivation agree.
'dotless' keeps the dot absent and gives up whatever the font view needs,
respecting slant: upright -> U+0131/U+0237, italic -> U+1D6A4/U+1D6A5.
'italic-dotless' forces U+1D6A4/U+1D6A5 whatever the record's style says,
for the families whose letters are inherently slanted.
Rules are tried IN ORDER and the first match wins, so the order is the
precedence.  'weight: bold' comes first deliberately: it overrides the
family rules below it.

rules.why: a bold cut is a weight of the styled letter, so the styled letter is what it should stay; this overrides the script and sans-serif rules below
blackboard bold and its italic/bold variants: losing 'double-struck' loses the only thing that identifies the font
fraktur and its variants, for the same reason
monospace is a width property, and width carries meaning in XML/HTML output, so it is not the thing to give up
script letters are inherently slanted, so the italic dotless character is the closest Unicode has; non-bold only -- the bold rule above catches bold script
calligraphic: CSS spells this family 'cursive' where MathML spells it 'script', and the same reasoning applies
non-bold sans-serif keeps the dot absent and respects slant, so upright gives U+0131/U+0237 and italic gives U+1D6A4/U+1D6A5

_default_why: no family to preserve, so nothing argues against keeping the dot absent
_about_rename: A dotless target needs the glyph RENAMED, and a dotted one does not.
Acrobat Distiller truncates a glyph name at the first dot before consulting
the AGL, so 'u1D48A.dtls' is read as 'u1D48A' -- which decodes to the letter
WITH its dot.  When the policy chose the dotted target that is the same
character the row already states, so truncation misrepresents nothing and no
rename is called for.  When it chose a dotless one the two disagree, and
without a rename the dotless cut would be published as the dotted letter.
The names below are the ones these fonts already use (stix-mathit-bold and
stix-mathsfit-bold carry them by hand).  Note they are NOT in the built-in
glyph list, so their job is to be dot-free and distinct rather than to carry
a codepoint -- the row's own codepoints do that.  'dotlessj' would be a trap
here: the built-in list maps it to U+F6BE, not to U+0237.
